title: Motion Verbs 6: Prefix у- (gone away)
description: The prefix у- attaches to идти / ехать and turns the verb perfective. The new meaning is 'gone away from the speaker's location': the subject is no longer here. Past forms only at this stage.
descriptionRussian: Приставка у- присоединяется к «идти» и «ехать» и делает глагол совершенного вида. Новое значение — «больше не здесь»: подлежащее покинуло место, в котором находится говорящий.
intro: The third prefix says the person is not here any more, which is a statement about absence rather than about the journey. It overlaps with the prefix from lesson 4, and the lesson is honest about that: both can describe the same departure. Which one you pick depends on whether you are reporting the leaving or the not-being-here.
rules: Уйти = perfective of идти; уехать = perfective of ехать. Both mark that the subject has gone away from the speaker's location: not here anymore.
Past forms today. On foot: ушёл / ушла / ушло / ушли (irregular). By transport: уехал / уехала / уехало / уехали (regular).
Source phrases choose у-: с + gen for work / class / surface (с работы, с урока), из + gen for buildings / cities (из дома, из Москвы). They do NOT pair with по-.
Other cues that pull у-: the adverb уже, an absence frame ('его здесь нет'), a long-absence duration ('на неделю,' 'надолго').
У- and по- often overlap. Stress absence → у-. Stress the moment of setting off → по-. Destination phrases в / на + acc still work with both.
examples: Антон уже ушёл с работы. (Anton has already left work.) С + gen source phrase + уже = pure absence focus.
Маша уехала в Петербург на неделю. (Masha has gone off to Petersburg for a week.) Long-absence duration phrase pulls у-.
Соня ушла из дома рано утром. (Sonya left the house early in the morning.) Из + gen source phrase + у-.
Дети ушли на урок час назад. (The kids left for class an hour ago.) Absence focus: they are gone, not here.
Иван уехал из Москвы вчера вечером. (Ivan left Moscow yesterday evening.) Из + gen pairs with у-, not with по-.
Лена уже ушла, я не успел с ней попрощаться. (Lena has already left; I did not get to say goodbye.) Absence-focus reading anchored by 'не успел.'

tables.title: У- vs по-: when each prefix wins

rows.label: уже + clause about absence
cells: Speaker reports the subject is not here anymore

rows.label: с / из + gen source phrase
cells: Source phrases do not pair with по-

rows.label: moment of departure as a clean event
cells: Speaker focuses on the act of setting off

rows.label: explicit time of departure ('в шесть')
cells: Both readings can fit; speaker's focus picks

rows.label: destination phrase в / на + acc
cells: Destination phrasing is unchanged from Lesson 3

items.prompt: Маша уже _____ из школы и сейчас дома.
items.promptEnglish: Masha has already arrived from school and is at home now.
items.hint: Recap from Lesson 5: 'из + gen' source plus the present-state 'сейчас дома' picks the arrival reading. Which form?
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 5: 'из школы' (gen source) + 'сейчас дома' (present state) = arrival on foot, fem → пришла. Today the same source-phrase syntax reappears with у- meaning 'left from,' but the warm-up keeps the L5 contrast in working memory.

items.prompt: Антон уже _____ , в офисе никого нет.
items.promptEnglish: Anton has already left; there is no one in the office.
items.hint: The empty office signals absence: he is no longer here. Which prefix marks 'gone away'?
items.explanation: 'В офисе никого нет' is the canonical absence frame: the speaker reports an empty room. У- carries that 'no longer here' reading: ушёл (masc past). Пошёл would mark the moment of departure as a clean event, neutral on whether the office is now empty. Шёл would describe him in motion mid-trip; пришёл would put him AT the destination. Only ушёл reports the absence.

items.prompt: Соня _____ с урока пораньше, потому что плохо себя чувствовала.
items.promptEnglish: Sonya left class early because she was feeling unwell.
items.hint: The 'с + gen' source phrase pairs cleanly with one prefix only. Which?
items.explanation: 'С урока' (gen source) is one of the source phrases that does not host по-. 'Пошла с урока' is awkward Russian; 'ушла с урока' is the standard form. Fem past of уйти → ушла. The reason clause is supporting; the form is fixed by the source phrase regardless.

items.prompt: Иван _____ в Петербург на неделю и вернётся в субботу.
items.promptEnglish: Ivan has gone off to Petersburg for a week and will be back on Saturday.
items.hint: 'На неделю' is a long-absence duration. Which transport prefix marks gone-away?
items.explanation: 'На неделю' frames a non-trivial absence: Ivan is gone for a stretch. The absence-focus reading + transport → уехал (у- prefix, masc). Поехал would report only the moment of setting off, not the absence; приехал would put him at Petersburg from Petersburg's perspective, not Moscow's; ехал would describe him in transit at some past moment. The 'вернётся в субботу' clause confirms a non-trivial absence ahead.

items.promptEnglish: The kids left for school an hour ago.
items.hint: 'Час назад' + the implicit 'they are not here' frame. Plural absence-focus on foot?
items.explanation: 'Час назад' is the time of departure relative to the speaker's now: an hour ago they left, and they are not back. Plural absence-focus on foot → ушли. Пошли would also be acceptable, but ушли more naturally hosts the 'не здесь' implication that час назад makes salient. The form пришли would say they have already arrived; шли would describe their motion mid-trip.

items.prompt: Лена _____ из города на машине рано утром.
items.promptEnglish: Lena drove out of town early in the morning.
items.hint: 'Из + gen' source pairs with one prefix only on transport. Which?
items.explanation: 'Из города' (gen source) is the same syntax as L5's 'из Москвы' but on the departure side. У- is the only natural choice with из + gen on transport: уехала. Поехала does not host an из-phrase cleanly; приехала would put her arriving at the city, not leaving it; ехала would describe motion mid-trip. The 'рано утром' phrase anchors the time; the form is fixed by the source phrase.

items.promptEnglish: Anton left work at six o'clock.
items.hint: The source phrase 'с работы' pairs with which prefix?
items.explanation: Departure from a source takes у-: ушёл с работы. Пошёл would mark setting off toward a destination; пришёл is the arrival; шёл is mid-walk.

items.hint: Gone away from a city, by transport, feminine.
items.explanation: Leaving a place behind takes у- on the transport verb: уехала из Москвы. Поехала marks setting off toward somewhere; приехала is arrival; ездила a round trip.

items.prompt: Лены здесь больше нет: она уже _____.
items.promptEnglish: Lena is no longer here: she has already left work.
items.hint: 'No longer here' is the absence reading.
items.explanation: The absence reading ('gone, not here') is exactly what у- encodes: ушла с работы. Пришла would mean she IS here; ходила would mean she went and came back.

items.promptEnglish: The parents went away to the seaside for a month.
items.hint: A long absence ('for a month') by transport.
items.explanation: The month-long absence takes у-: уехали на море на месяц. Поехали reports only the departure moment; ездили would mean the trip is already over; приехали с моря is a return.

items.promptEnglish: The children left the house early in the morning.
items.hint: Из + gen source on foot, plural.
items.explanation: The из-source departure takes у-: ушли из дома. Пришли is arrival; шли is mid-walk; ходили would claim a round trip already completed.

blanks: Маша _____ на дачу на выходные. (Masha has gone off to the dacha for the weekend.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: 'На выходные' frames a long-absence duration: she will be at the dacha through the weekend. Absence-focus on transport, fem → уехала. Поехала would mark the moment of departure as a clean event without stressing the absence; ездила would imply a completed there-and-back, contradicting 'на выходные'; ехала would describe her on the road at some past moment.

minimalPairs.context: Маша уже _____ , я не успел с ней попрощаться.
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Masha has already left; I did not get to say goodbye.
minimalPairs.explanation: 'Уже...Не успел попрощаться' frames absence: Masha is no longer here, and the speaker missed the goodbye window. У- carries that reading: ушла (fem past). Шла would describe her in motion at some past moment, which cannot host the 'не успел попрощаться' frame; the speaker would have caught her on the way out, not missed her.

minimalPairs.context: Иван _____ в Москву и сейчас живёт там.
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Ivan went off to Moscow and now lives there.
minimalPairs.explanation: 'Сейчас живёт там' rules out a completed round-trip: Ivan is in Moscow and has not returned. Absence-focus on transport → уехал (у- prefix, masc). Ездил would mean he went and came back, contradicting the present-tense 'живёт там.'

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The guests left the city in the morning.
errorCorrection.explanation: Source phrases (из + gen) pair with у-: уехали из города. 'Поехали из города' is awkward, because по- reports the moment of setting off toward a destination, not departure from a source. Приехали is the arrival, the opposite end.

errorCorrection.sentence: Дети ушли в школу и сидят на уроке.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The children arrived at school and are sitting in class.
errorCorrection.explanation: 'Сидят на уроке' reports the children's present state at school: they are there now, in class. The arrival reading carries that frame: пришли (Lesson 5). Ушли would imply they are no longer at the speaker's location, which contradicts the next clause anchoring them at school. Шли is motion in progress; ходили a completed round-trip.

errorCorrection.sentence: Иван ушёл в Москву на неделю.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Ivan has gone off to Moscow for a week.
errorCorrection.explanation: Уйти is the on-foot member; уехать is the transport member. Moscow is far too distant for on-foot travel, so the transport prefix is required: уехал. The destination 'в Москву' and the long-absence 'на неделю' both fit уехать (gone away by transport). Поехал would stress only the moment of setting off; приехал would mean arriving in Moscow.

errorCorrection.sentence: Антон ездил в командировку и ещё не вернулся.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Anton has gone away on a business trip and hasn't come back yet.
errorCorrection.explanation: 'Ещё не вернулся' (hasn't come back yet) shows Anton is still away, so the absence reading: уехал (у- prefix). Ездил means a completed there-and-back trip, which directly contradicts 'hasn't returned'. Ехал would describe him in transit at a past moment; приехал would mean he has arrived back, also contradicting the unfinished absence.

reviewVocab.definition: Perfective verbs formed with у- + идти / ехать. They mark that the subject has gone away from the speaker's location: not here anymore. Past forms ушёл / уехал are the workhorses at this stage.

The 'gone-away' prefix in the motion-verb system. Attached to идти / ехать it produces perfective verbs of departure focused on the subject's absence. It overlaps with по- (Lesson 4) but adds an absence focus and pairs with source phrases.
reviewVocab.example: Маша уехала в Петербург на неделю.

reviewVocab.definition: The preposition с taking the genitive to name a source: surfaces, work, classes, lectures (с работы, с урока, с лекции). Pairs with у- to mark departure from one of those places. Mirror of на + acc destination phrases (на работу, на урок, на лекцию).
